questions.q: What kind of workload does Athena serve in this capstone, versus Redshift?
options: Ad hoc, one-off questions that don't justify a scheduled load, queried directly against the Glue Catalog
The exact same scheduled dashboard queries as Redshift, duplicated for redundancy
Only queries against Redshift tables, never S3 directly
Writing new data into the curated zone
questions.explain: Athena is used for ad hoc analyst questions that don't deserve a permanent table or scheduled load; Redshift serves the repeated dashboard workload.

questions.q: What does Athena bill for, and how does the northfield-analysts workgroup guard against runaway cost?
options: It bills per byte scanned, and the workgroup sets a 5 GB per-query scan limit
It bills a flat monthly fee regardless of usage
It bills per query regardless of size, with no guardrails possible
It bills per row returned, capped at 1,000 rows per query
questions.explain: Athena's billing unit is bytes scanned; northfield-analysts sets a 5 GB per-query scan limit as a cost guardrail.

questions.q: In the top-products-by-region query, why does filtering WHERE dt BETWEEN ... reduce cost?
options: It prunes partitions, so Athena skips scanning any dt partition outside the requested range entirely
It has no effect on cost, only on result ordering
It forces Athena to use Redshift instead of scanning S3
It only affects which columns are returned, not bytes scanned
questions.explain: Because the table is partitioned by dt, a WHERE dt filter lets Athena prune partitions outside the range, scanning far fewer bytes.

questions.q: Why does querying northfield_orders_curated (Parquet) typically cost less than querying the equivalent raw CSV?
options: Parquet is columnar, so a query needing only a few columns reads just those column chunks instead of every column of every row
Parquet files are always smaller in total file count
CSV cannot be queried by Athena at all
Curated data has fewer rows than raw data
questions.explain: Column pruning is only possible with a columnar format like Parquet; CSV has no column-level structure to skip, so every column of every row gets scanned.

questions.q: How does northfield_orders_curated get registered in the Glue Data Catalog, given there's no crawler for the curated zone?
options: The Glue ETL job's sink sets enableUpdateCatalog=True, so writing the Parquet output also registers/updates the catalog table
It must be created manually in the Athena console before every query
Athena creates it automatically the first time it's queried
It is copied over from northfield_orders_raw with no changes
questions.explain: Lesson 5's ETL job uses enableUpdateCatalog=True on its Glue sink, so the same write both produces the Parquet files and updates the Catalog table.
